title: Presidential Transition Enhancement Act of 2019
official_summary:
Presidential Transition Enhancement Act of 2019

This bill makes changes intended to smooth the transfer of executive power during presidential transitions.

The bill provides for the detailing of legislative branch employees on a reimbursable basis to office staffs designated by the President-elect or Vice President-elect with the consent of the supervising Member of Congress.

The bill extends support provided by the General Services Administration (GSA) to the President- and Vice President-elect for up to 60 days after the inauguration.

By September 1 of a year during which a presidential election occurs, the GSA shall enter into a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with each eligible candidate, which shall include the conditions for administrative support services and facilities. To the maximum extent practicable, an MOU shall be based on MOUs relating to previous presidential transitions. Each MOU shall include an agreement that the eligible candidate will implement and enforce an ethics plan to guide the conduct of the transition beginning on the date on which such candidate becomes President-elect. The plan shall be published on the GSA website.

By September 15 of a year during which a presidential election occurs, each agency shall ensure that a succession plan is in place for each senior noncareer position in the agency.

summary.headline: This law sets up rules to help the incoming and outgoing presidential administrations hand off power more smoothly.
summary.what_it_does: It lets the President-elect and Vice President-elect get temporary staff detailed from Congress, paid back on a reimbursable basis, with the consent of the lawmaker who supervises them. It extends federal General Services Administration support to these officials for up to 60 days after inauguration. In election years, GSA must sign a written agreement with each eligible candidate by September 1 covering administrative services and facilities, and that agreement must include an ethics plan that is published on the GSA website. Agencies must also make sure each senior noncareer position has a succession plan by September 15 of an election year.

who_it_affects.how: They can receive detailed congressional staff and extended GSA support, and they must agree to follow and enforce a published ethics plan.
They must sign a memorandum of understanding with GSA by September 1 of an election year that sets the conditions for transition support.
Legislative branch employees may be detailed to presidential transition offices with their supervising Member's consent.

who_it_affects.group: Senior noncareer federal employees and their agencies
who_it_affects.how: Each agency must have a succession plan in place for every senior noncareer position by September 15 of an election year.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 3, 2020; the MOU and succession plan deadlines apply in years when a presidential election occurs.
